title: THE ZW1215 CASE STUDY -- the one cluster where the P4 falsifier fires
doc: profile (slope, kTvir, M500, f_gas(420), a0-crossing, r_M, gas-vs-dark), the three candidates, the decision with the committed data alone, verdicts V1-V3 with the deciding number

constants.T(r)_provenance: T(r) read from the G105 cache of the OFFICIAL X-COP release (Ghirardini+19 A&A 621 A41; G105 V0b md5 gate 12/12)

literature_flags: Laganá, Durret & Lopes 2019, MNRAS 484, 2807 (arXiv:1901.03851), Table 2: ZwCl1215 in the NCC-DISTURBED group; 2D maps 'disturbed'; NCC by 3/6 CC criteria
Lovisari et al. 2017, ApJ 846, 51 (arXiv:1708.02590), Table H1: state 'M'; c = 0.16 +/- 0.01 (at the relaxed cut c > 0.15); w = (0.45 +/- 0.02)e-2 (relaxed class)
Ghirardini et al. 2019, A&A 621, A41 (official X-COP release, md5-verified in G105): ZW1215 T(r) flat, no central cool-core drop

Eckert et al. 2019, A&A 621, A40, Table 2: f_gas,500(HSE) = 0.106 +/- 0.008 and f_gas,200 = 0.092 +/- 0.009, both the LOWEST of the 12; 'With just two exceptions (A3266 and ZwCl 1215), the gas fraction of all systems is at least as large as our determination of the Universal gas fraction'
Sereno et al. 2024, A&A 682, A147, Table B.2: ZwCl1215.1+0400 M_lens(CoMaLit) = 3.50 +/- 2.20 e14 vs M_HSE(XMM) = 5.63 +/- 0.57 e14 -> M_lens/M_HSE = 0.62 +/- 0.40

a_hydrostatic_bias.reading: fall lives in the M_FORW denominator slope; published disturbance flags present; outer f_gas the sample's lowest; case not proof (no direct WL mass PROFILE)

b_gas_concentration_inversion.direction: larger r_c -> shallower gas -> larger s_g -> MORE positive d ln f_gas/d ln r (amplified rise, not fall)
b_gas_concentration_inversion.magnitude: r_half_gas = 841 kpc vs sample median 800 kpc (rank 8/12); s_g = 1.445 vs median 1.536

c_phantom_share_edge.direction: high phantom share (d ln M_ph/d ln r = 1) slows the dark's growth -> accelerates the rise (wrong sign)
c_phantom_share_edge.magnitude: s_ph(420) = 0.241 vs sample median 0.288 (rank 9/12, high=1): dust-dominated side

candidates.decision: with the committed data alone, (a) survives; the discriminating profile feature is the denominator: the same cluster is flat on the M_NFW footing (slope +0.027 vs -0.067 on M_HSE)

V1_discriminating_feature.feature: d ln M_gas/d ln r < d ln M_HSE/d ln r in-window (s_g 1.445 vs s_t 1.525; the one positive gap of 12), with the fall carried by the M_FORW denominator (flat on M_NFW: +0.027)

V3_honest_statement.deciding_number: footing contrast slope(M_HSE) - slope(M_NFW) = -0.093; P(most extreme of 12 <= -0.067) = 0.29
V3_honest_statement.text: the falsifier fires on ZW1215 with a precise monotone fall (-0.067 +/- 0.007, 9.8 sigma from zero) -- not a breakdown of the rise as such (11/12 rise; the cluster is FLAT on the M_NFW footing, +0.027) and not a fluke of the profile; the fall is entirely the hydrostatic denominator's (Delta = -0.093), in the one cluster the literature flags as NCC-disturbed with the sample's lowest f_gas -- a hydrostatic-bias-class case, provisional (no direct WL mass profile exists; P(min<=fall) = 0.29 keeps the population-level fluke reading alive)

checks.name: A0 [gate: G107's committed ZW1215 row reproduced] slope -0.067 +/- 0.007, monotone (Spearman < -0.9), 18 in-window bins
checks.reading: the lane reads the SAME committed FITS with the SAME recipe as G107; the fall: f_gas(0.2 R500) = 0.165 -> f_gas(R500) = 0.148

checks.name: A1a [the inner end is sample-ordinary] ZW1215's f_gas(420) within 0.03 of the sample median
checks.reading: the fall is NOT an inner-excess: the inner gas fraction sits at the sample's typical level (caveat: A3266's fgas table ends at 0.79 R500 -- its window and R500-end values come from the in-window fit, as in G107)

checks.name: A1b [the outer end is gas-poor] ZW1215's f_gas(R500) in the sample's bottom third (rank <= 4/12)
checks.reading: the fall is driven by the OUTER end: the outer gas fraction is the sample's lowest-or-second-lowest -- the hydrostatic denominator grows too fast with radius in ZW1215

checks.name: A2a [the a0-crossing: does ZW1215 have one?] finite crossing on the committed M_FORW profile (G057's 'none' class = A1644, A2255)
checks.measured: ZW1215 a0-crossing = 752 kpc = 0.55 R500 (in-window); no-crossing class: ['A1644', 'A2255']; sample median 703 kpc
checks.reading: ZW1215 is NOT in the no-crossing class: its measured total field crosses a0 at 0.55 R500, inside the window -- the fall is not the absence of a field transition

checks.name: A2b [r_M and the rise-scale] r_M = sqrt(G M_b(R500)/a0) and the 50%-point r_half for the ZW1215 profile
checks.measured: r_M = 420 kpc; r_half = 594 kpc (r_half/r_M = 1.41; the sample median r_half/r_M = 1.43)
checks.reading: the 50%-point of the (falling) profile sits at the r_M-class like the other 10 -- the crossover SCALE is not the anomaly; the ANOMALY is the sign of the slope

checks.name: A3a [the mechanics inversion] ZW1215 is one of at most TWO clusters where d ln M_gas/d ln r < d ln M_HSE/d ln r in-window (median gap), and the only one of those with a FALLING f_gas slope (<= -0.05): the fall is mechanically the denominator outgrowing the gas
checks.measured: ZW1215: s_g = 1.445 vs s_t = 1.525, gap = +0.080; clusters with gap >= 0: ['A2029', 'ZW1215'] (A2029's gap is +0.076 with slope +0.104 -- flat, not the falsifier)
checks.reading: the fall is the ONE positive-gap profile with a slope <= -0.05: the enclosed gas grows slower than the hydrostatic total through the whole window -- mechanically forced, not an endpoint artefact; A2029 shares the positive median gap but its OLS slope is flat

checks.name: A3b [the phantom share at 420 kpc] ZW1215's s_ph(420) FLOOR-A share vs the sample (was ZW1215 the most phantom-dominated?)
checks.reading: ZW1215 is NOT the most phantom-dominated: it sits BELOW the sample median (dust-dominated side) -- and directionally a HIGH phantom share would slow the dark's growth (phantom d ln M/d ln r = 1) and ACCELERATE the rise, the wrong sign for the fall; candidate (c) fails

checks.name: B2 [candidate (b) REFUTED] (i) the direction argument is algebraic: a larger r_c -> shallower gas -> larger s_g -> MORE positive d ln f_gas/d ln r (an amplified RISE, never a fall); (ii) in-cluster the premise is inverted: ZW1215's gas is MORE concentrated than its dark (s_g < s_t, the fall's own requirement); (iii) absolutely, ZW1215's gas is unremarkable: r_half_gas at the sample-median class
checks.measured: in-cluster ordering s_g = 1.445 vs s_t = 1.525 (gas steeper than dark); r_half_gas(ZW1215) = 841 kpc = 0.62 R500 vs median 800 kpc (0.59 R500-class), rank 8/12
checks.reading: candidate (b) fails: 'baryons less concentrated than the dark' cannot produce a fall (it amplifies the rise), the committed profile shows the OPPOSITE in-cluster ordering (gas MORE concentrated than dark), and the absolute gas concentration is not an outlier (0.62 vs 0.60 R500, the 8th smallest of 12 = the 5th largest)

checks.name: C [the decision] exactly one candidate survives the committed data: (a), with (b) and (c) failing on direction and magnitude as quantified above
checks.measured: survivor = (a) hydrostatic bias; (b) FAIL (r_half_gas 841 vs med 800; direction wrong); (c) FAIL (s_ph(420) 0.241 vs med 0.288; direction wrong)
checks.reading: the decision is a profile-level statement: the fall's support is the hydrostatic-denominator slope, and every published flag of this cluster points to the bias class

checks.name: D1 [V1 -- the discriminating feature] the fall is (i) precise and monotone on M_HSE (-0.067 +/- 0.007, 18 bins, Spearman -0.95), (ii) carried by the DENOMINATOR (flat on M_NFW: +0.027), and (iii) driven by the OUTER end (f_gas(R500) rank 2/12)
checks.reading: the discriminating profile feature: the same cluster is flat on the papers' NFW denominator -- the fall is a property of the hydrostatic mass profile's radial slope (the outer M_FORW grows too fast), i.e. of the mass side a non-equilibrium gas state would corrupt

checks.name: D2 [V2 -- the surviving candidate] (a) the hydrostatic bias (non-equilibrium gas state: merger/AGN/heating), with (b) and (c) failing as quantified in B2/B3 and C
checks.measured: survivor = (a); published flags: Laganá+19 NCC-disturbed, Lovisari+17 'M' (c = 0.16, w = 4.5e-3), Eckert+19 f_gas,500 = 0.106 (lowest), Sereno+24 M_lens/M_HSE = 0.62 +/- 0.40
checks.reading: (a) is a case, not a proof: consistent with every committed profile and every published flag, but no direct WL mass-profile of ZwCl1215 exists to measure the bias

checks.name: D1b [the official-release T(r)] ZW1215's central temperature is flat (no cool-core dip) -- the NCC heating/merger state
checks.reading: a cool core shows T(0.05)/T(0.35) well below 1 (central drop); ZW1215's ~1.0 flat profile is the NCC signature -- the gas is not in the relaxed cooling-core state

checks.name: V3 [the honest statement] the falsifier fires on ZW1215: a precise monotone fall on the committed M_HSE definition (-0.067 +/- 0.007) that is flat on the M_NFW footing (+0.027) -- the deciding number is the footing contrast Delta = -0.093: the fall is the hydrostatic denominator's, in the one cluster the literature flags as NCC-disturbed with the sample's lowest f_gas
checks.measured: breakdown? no (rise holds 11/12, pooled +0.250); fluke? P(min<=-0.067) = 0.29 (population level), not for the profile (9.8 sigma); bias case: consistent, not measured
checks.reading: V3 is the honest statement the task asks for: the falsifier performs its designed function -- it names the one cluster where the M_HSE reading fails -- and that cluster carries independent published flags of the non-equilibrium/heating class; the NFW footing shows the failure is not the gas-vs-baryon structure
